q: Computable analysis extends computability to real functions. A real function f: ℝ → ℝ is computable (in the sense of Turing-Weihrauch) if:
opts: There is a Turing machine that, given a rational approximation to x within 2^{-n}, outputs a rational approximation to f(x) within 2^{-n}
It maps computable reals to computable reals
exp: Computable real functions: f is computable if a TM can convert ε-approximations of x into δ-approximations of f(x) uniformly in ε. This is strictly stronger than continuity. Computable functions are continuous, but not all continuous functions are computable.
